## Verdict

## Bearer

RaceRepositoryImpl — core-data/src/main/kotlin/com/mgilli/core/data/race/RaceRepositoryImpl.kt, function `persist`

Second symbol (a second gap, not following from the first): `HyresultResultParser` — core-domain/src/main/kotlin/com/mgilli/core/domain/race/HyresultResultParser.kt, private val `EXPECTED_LABELS` / function `buildExpectedLabels`.

## Trigger

`persist` runs on every race write reachable through the public
repository functions — `saveImportedRace`, `saveRecordedRace`,
`replaceReference` — observed.

For the second symbol: `EXPECTED_LABELS` is computed once, eagerly, at
`HyresultResultParser`'s object initialisation — triggered by the
first reference to the object (e.g. any call to `parse`) — observed.

## Today

`persist` writes the race and its children via `raceDao.upsert`, then
re-reads it with `raceDao.findById(raceId)!!` to build the returned
`Race`. If the row is not there right after the write — a rolled-back
transaction, a concurrent delete between the write and the re-read —
this throws a `NullPointerException` instead of failing gracefully.
`persist` is called from `saveImportedRace`, `saveRecordedRace` and
`replaceReference`, all of which otherwise return `Result` and are
documented (TECHNICAL_CONVENTIONS §13: "A repository returns a result
type, never null on failure") to never surface a raw crash on failure.

Separately, `HyresultResultParser.buildExpectedLabels` calls
`SegmentBlueprint.stationAt(index)!!` for every index it identifies as
`SegmentType.STATION`. `stationAt` returns `Station?`, non-null only
where `SegmentBlueprint.typeAt` reports `STATION` — a contract stated
only in `stationAt`'s doc comment, never enforced by a type or a test.
Because `EXPECTED_LABELS` is a `private val` evaluated at class load,
any future change to `SegmentBlueprint.typeAt` or `stationAt` that
breaks this pairing crashes the object's static initialiser — no
caller, no stack frame naming a race or a parse call, just
`HyresultResultParser` failing to load.

## Expected

`persist` (and the callers that rely on it) no longer let the
post-write re-read crash the process: a row absent after `upsert`
completes as a `Result.failure`, propagated out of `saveImportedRace`,
`saveRecordedRace` and `replaceReference` the same way `setAsReference`,
`rename` and `delete` already report a missing row — per §13, never a
raw null-caused crash.

`HyresultResultParser` and `SegmentBlueprint` have their pairing
checked by something other than a runtime `!!` at class load: either
`buildExpectedLabels` is written so a `STATION` index with no station
fails predictably with a message naming the index, or a test in
`core-domain` (per §14, "the import parser is tested against a real
captured result") asserts that every `STATION` index blueprint pairs
with a `stationAt` value, so the two files cannot drift silently.
